Margin Support

A calm podcast player that shows where your time goes

Email: brendan@everlight-digital.com · Privacy

About Margin

Margin is a podcast player for people who listen a lot and want to stay in charge of it. It has per-show speed and skip settings, silence trimming, an Inbox for new episodes, multiple queues, chapters, transcripts, and stats about how you listen. No account, no ads, no tracking.

Shows & episodes

Why does a show have video in Apple Podcasts but not in Margin?

Since 2026, Apple gets video for some shows privately from the show's host. That video does not travel through the public feed that every podcast app reads, so Margin never sees it.

Margin plays video whenever a show's public feed includes it. Those episodes show a Video tag.

To get a show's video here, ask the show to add its video to its public feed.

I can't find a show. How do I add it?

In Library, tap the round menu button with three dots at the top right, then tap Find a show. Search by name. If it doesn't turn up, paste the show's feed address, an Apple Podcasts link, or a Spotify link into the Link box and tap Add.

Some shows live only on Spotify and have no public feed. Margin can't add those.

A show isn't showing new episodes. What can I do?

Pull down on the Library screen to check every show for new episodes. You can also pull down on a single show's page to check just that show.

Margin also checks for new episodes by itself now and then, but iOS decides exactly when it gets to run. If a show still looks stuck, the show's host may not have published the episode yet.

How do I get new episodes without losing track of them?

New episodes that Margin finds when it checks a show wait in the Inbox tab. For each one you can tap Next or Last to put it in your queue, or Remove to take it out of the Inbox. Removed episodes stay in your library and are not marked played.

Open a show, then Playback settings, to keep that show out of the Inbox or to send only its newest few. In Inbox settings you can have episodes leave the Inbox on their own after a day, three days, a week, two weeks, or a month. Never is the default.

To have episodes downloaded before you open the app, go to Settings, then Auto-download new episodes. Choose Off, Latest 1, 2, 5, or 10, or All. It is off by default, and each show can pick its own from its page or from By show. Downloads wait for Wi-Fi unless you turn Wi-Fi only off.

Your library

How do I bring my shows in from another app?

From Apple Podcasts: open Settings, tap Add the Shortcut once, then tap Run the import. The Shortcut reads the shows you follow on this iPhone and hands them to Margin. Nothing is unfollowed in Apple Podcasts, and your place in each episode stays there.

From other apps: export your subscriptions as an OPML file (most podcast apps can do this), then tap Import OPML in Settings and choose the file.

From Spotify: tap Import from Spotify in Settings for step-by-step help using your Spotify data download.

Does Margin sync between my devices?

Yes, if you turn it on. Sync with iCloud (beta) is off by default. When you switch it on in Settings, your library, queue, and listening history sync to your own private iCloud. Nothing is sent anywhere else, and there is no Margin account.

The change takes effect the next time you quit and reopen the app.

My library isn't syncing. What can I check?

Make sure Sync with iCloud (beta) is on in Settings on every device, and quit and reopen Margin after you change it. Each device needs to be signed in to the same Apple Account with iCloud turned on.

If iCloud sync can't start, Margin says so under the switch in Settings and keeps your data on that device only. Nothing is lost.

If it still won't sync, email us. Say which devices you have and what the message under the switch says.

Can I take my data with me?

Yes. In Settings, Export OPML saves your list of shows to a file you can bring to another podcast app. Export listening data gives you your listening sessions as a spreadsheet file (CSV) and everything else as a JSON file.

These files are made on your iPhone and are not uploaded. You choose where they go: Files, AirDrop, Mail, or another app.

CarPlay, Apple Watch & widgets

Does Margin work with CarPlay, Apple Watch, widgets, and Siri?

Yes.

CarPlay: Margin has a CarPlay screen with Up Next, Shows, and Recent.

Apple Watch: Margin has a watch app. It plays episodes stored on the watch and works as a remote for what is playing on your iPhone. In Settings, then Apple Watch, you can send your next 3 or 5 downloaded Up Next episodes to the watch. Only downloaded episodes are sent.

Widgets: add Now Playing, Listening Today, or Up Next to your Home Screen. Touch and hold the Home Screen, tap the plus button, and choose Margin. On iOS 18 and later you can also add Play / Pause and Skip Forward controls to Control Center or the Lock Screen.

Siri and Shortcuts: Margin has actions to play, pause, skip, play a show, play Up Next, add a show to Up Next, and set or turn off the sleep timer.

Transcripts

Where do transcripts come from?

If a show publishes its own transcript, Margin downloads it. If not, on iPhones that support it, your iPhone makes one itself using Apple's on-device speech recognition. Your audio is never uploaded.

By default, Margin does this while your iPhone is charging, for episodes in Up Next and shows you listen to most. You can also allow it on battery in Settings, then Transcripts.

It waits while you are listening, when your iPhone is warm, and in Low Power Mode.

By default, Margin also uses a shared transcript cache so other listeners get transcripts faster. When your iPhone has a finished transcript for a public show, it sends that transcript text and a one-way code for the episode. In the background it also asks the cache for transcripts of episodes from your shows, using the same code. It never sends your audio, your name, or private feeds. You can turn this off in Settings, then Transcripts.

Privacy & support

Do I need an account?

No. Margin has no sign-in at all. Sync, if you turn it on, uses your own private iCloud.

What does Margin know about me?

Margin has no account, no ads, and no analytics.

One feature uses Margin's own server: the shared transcript cache, on by default for public shows. It sends finished transcripts and a one-way code for each episode, never your name, account, audio, or private feeds. Turn it off in Settings, then Transcripts.

Your library and listening history stay on your iPhone. If you turn on iCloud sync, they also go into your own private iCloud, which only you can read.
